summary: rasterkit shadows the Pillow (PIL) top-level namespace and ships a dormant BMP-tail stego decoder
details: The distribution is published as 'rasterkit' but installs its modules under the top-level 'PIL' package (top_level.txt = 'PIL'), shipping PIL/__init__.py, PIL/Image.py, PIL/_binary.py, and a PIL/_data/ tree. Installed alongside the real Pillow, it collides with and can shadow the upstream Pillow package on sys.path, so 'from PIL import Image' resolves to code shipped by this publisher rather than upstream Pillow. In addition, PIL/_binary.py defines bmp_plane_tail(), which reads a trailing window of bytes from a BMP, XORs each byte with a caller-supplied 'mix' key, and splits the result into arbitrary segments; PIL/_data/__init__.py hardcodes matching demo constants (DEMO_TAIL_COUNT=5092, DEMO_TAIL_MIX=42, DEMO_TAIL_SEGMENTS=[3379, 1713]) and ships a paired demo.bmp payload carrier. The extracted bytes are only returned to callers in this version — no exec, compile, subprocess, or network sink consumes them — and no lifecycle hook or import-time side effect triggers the decoder, so installing v1.0.4 does not itself execute a payload. The XOR-tail-split shape has no legitimate imaging purpose and, combined with the PIL namespace shadowing, is prepositioned infrastructure that a future release under the same distribution name could weaponize by adding a loader that runs the decoded bytes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
